title: Creative Hub funding and Community Benefits Charge direction
subtitle: Also: Aud signing authority, natural gas purchase policy, tribunal appointments and Manchester Road traffic calming.
overview: The Finance and Corporate Services Committee made recommendations to Council on six items. The most discussed was the 44 Gaukel Creative Hub. The committee recommended that staff prepare a 2024 budget issue paper for ongoing operating funds and study long-term location options for the 2025 budget process {{vote:m2}}.

The committee also recommended that staff develop a Community Benefits Charge strategy and by-law {{vote:m3}}. Staff said the charge would raise relatively little and would need a consultant, and that it could be appealed. One councillor said they may seek a deferral at Council while the province's Bill 23 funding response remains unclear.

Other recommendations: delegated authority for The Aud's manager and the Director of Sport to sign talent, suite and sponsorship agreements {{vote:m1}}; updates to the Gas Purchase Policy {{vote:m4}}; three councillors to sit on the Licensing Appeal Tribunal {{vote:m5}}; and a traffic calming plan for Manchester Road {{vote:m6}}. Council will consider these later.

decisions.detail: The committee recommended staff prepare a 2024 budget issue paper for annual operating funds and assess long-term location options for the 2025 budget process {{vote:m2}}.
The committee recommended that staff develop a Community Benefits Charge strategy and by-law {{vote:m3}}.
The committee recommended authorizing the Aud's manager to sign talent, suite and sponsorship agreements, and the Director of Sport to sign sponsorship agreements, within set parameters {{vote:m1}}.
The committee recommended approving the updates to Policy FIN-ACQ-560, Gas Purchase Policy {{vote:m4}}.
The committee recommended implementing the proposed traffic calming plan for Manchester Road {{vote:m6}}.
The committee recommended appointing Councillors P. Singh, S. Davey and A. Owodunni as tribunal members {{vote:m5}}.

debate: Delegates from the Creative Hub's operating partner, an arts program and a music studio said the hub is full with a waitlist, gives artists affordable shared space and supports local business. One tenant said it helps keep talent in Kitchener and asked for better soundproofing.

Councillors asked how the Creative Hub could grow, with ideas including digital media and rehearsal space, other funding sources, and better data on its economic impact. One councillor said growth would have to compete with other financial pressures at the next budget.

On the Community Benefits Charge, staff said it is a supplement to development charges. It is capped at 4% of land value, applies only to larger developments, and needs a consultant and valuations. Staff added that it has been appealed in about half of the municipalities that adopted it.

Some councillors questioned spending on a consultant before the province clarifies how it will make municipalities whole under Bill 23. Others wanted to move ahead and focus the charge on parkland, affordable housing and existing parks. Staff said the consultant's expertise is needed for a complex framework and that waiting carries little risk.

On the gas policy, one councillor asked about the 20-year transportation contract term amid climate uncertainty. Staff said 20 years is typical and shorter terms could be considered. Staff also confirmed that the 50% cap on purchases from any one supplier applies to all suppliers.
